_source: City of St. Petersburg Land Development Regulations (LDR), Chapter 16 — Zoning Districts. Verify all standards against current adopted code at stpete.org/ldr

DC-1.name: Downtown Center
DC-1.allowed_uses_summary: Residential, hotel, office, retail, restaurant, entertainment, civic — full mix of uses
DC-1.notes: Build-to lines apply per the Downtown Streetscape Plan. Height up to 400 ft; specific limits vary by sub-area — confirm with CDB/Planning. FAR bonuses available through CRA and TDR programs. Design standards required. Verify current sub-district height maps with City of St. Pete Planning.

DC-2.name: Downtown Connector
DC-2.allowed_uses_summary: Mixed-use: residential, office, retail, hotel along linear connecting corridors
DC-2.notes: Connects downtown core to adjacent neighborhoods. Build-to lines apply. Stepbacks above certain floor heights may be required per design standards.

DC-3.name: Downtown Neighborhood
DC-3.allowed_uses_summary: Residential, limited neighborhood-scale retail and office; transitional downtown edge
DC-3.notes: Transitional zone between downtown core and residential neighborhoods. Design standards apply.

DC-4.name: Downtown Edge
DC-4.allowed_uses_summary: Predominantly residential with small-scale neighborhood commercial at ground floor
DC-4.notes: Outer edge of the downtown zoning overlay. Designed to preserve neighborhood character while allowing modest intensification.

NT-1.name: Neighborhood Traditional 1
NT-1.allowed_uses_summary: Single-family residential; accessory dwelling units per LDR
NT-1.notes: Most restrictive single-family neighborhood district. Preserves traditional lot patterns. Verify minimum lot area with specific sub-area standards in the LDR.

NT-2.name: Neighborhood Traditional 2
NT-2.allowed_uses_summary: Single-family and duplex residential; ADUs permitted
NT-2.notes: Single-family with limited residential intensification. Duplexes permitted on qualifying lots.

NT-3.name: Neighborhood Traditional 3
NT-3.allowed_uses_summary: Single-family, duplex, triplex, townhouses; higher residential density
NT-3.notes: Higher-intensity traditional neighborhood district allowing small attached residential. Per-unit lot area applies.

NE.name: Neighborhood Edge
NE.allowed_uses_summary: Multi-family residential, limited neighborhood commercial; transitional between residential and commercial corridors
NE.notes: Transitional district at the edge of residential neighborhoods adjacent to commercial corridors.

NMX.name: Neighborhood Mixed Use
NMX.allowed_uses_summary: Ground-floor retail/service, upper-floor residential or office; neighborhood-serving commercial
NMX.notes: Encourages pedestrian-oriented neighborhood commercial nodes. Ground floor active use required on primary street frontage.

CMX-1.name: Commercial Mixed Use 1
CMX-1.allowed_uses_summary: Retail, office, personal service, residential above ground floor; neighborhood and community commercial
CMX-1.notes: Lower-intensity commercial corridor district. Active ground floor street frontage standards apply. Parking requirements may be reduced in certain overlay areas.

CMX-2.name: Commercial Mixed Use 2
CMX-2.allowed_uses_summary: Broad mix of retail, office, hotel, multi-family residential; community-scale commercial
CMX-2.notes: Mid-intensity commercial mixed-use. Design standards for streetwall and ground floor activation. Taller buildings may require stepbacks above certain floors.

CMX-3.name: Commercial Mixed Use 3
CMX-3.allowed_uses_summary: High-intensity mixed use: major retail, office, hotel, residential; regional commercial nodes
CMX-3.notes: Highest-intensity commercial mixed-use zone outside downtown. Regional-scale uses permitted. Stepback requirements above certain floor heights. Design review required.

IL.name: Industrial Light
IL.allowed_uses_summary: Light manufacturing, warehouse, flex office, research and development, limited retail
IL.notes: Light industrial uses compatible with adjacent residential or commercial areas. Outdoor storage limited. Buffering required adjacent to residential.

IG.name: Industrial General
IG.allowed_uses_summary: General manufacturing, warehousing, heavy commercial, utility facilities
IG.notes: General industrial district. Outdoor storage permitted with screening. Heavier uses require additional buffering and review.

P.name: Public / Quasi-Public
P.allowed_uses_summary: Government facilities, civic uses, schools, hospitals, parks, utilities, places of worship
P.notes: Standards vary by specific use and CDB approval. Institutional uses may exceed height with special exception. Confirm requirements with City of St. Pete Planning.

BP.name: Business Park
BP.allowed_uses_summary: Office, flex office, limited light manufacturing, R&D; campus-style employment
BP.notes: Intended for campus employment environments. Landscaping and design standards apply. Retail limited to serving on-site employees.
